style_guide: Quiet, cinematic late-night meditation that shifts gently into reverent, painterly devotional art. Master aspect 4:5, with a safe-centred composition so it can be reframed to 9:16. Palette: deep midnight and indigo blues, cool smartphone cyan, a soft moonlight silver, and a faint warm amber from distant city lights. The single devotional scene uses dawn tones of pale gold, peach and soft sky blue. Lighting is low-key and soft, with gentle falloff, no harsh contrast and a subtle filmic grain. Camera work is slow and unhurried: gentle push-ins, locked-off frames, slow time-lapse drift. No fast cuts and no shake. Lenses: 50–85mm shallow depth of field for the intimate bedroom shots, 24–35mm wide for the skies. Real-world scenes are photorealistic and painterly at the edges, while the Krishna–Arjuna scene is a traditional, reverent painting style inspired by classical Indian miniature and devotional art. The mood is tender, calm, non-judgemental and spacious, with lots of negative space for captions added in editing. No people's faces are visible in the modern scenes. Never render any text, letters, Devanagari, UI or logos inside generated frames. All on-screen text and the Echoes of Gita mark are added in editing.

assets.prompt: Photorealistic cinematic close-up of a dim bedroom at 1 a.m. A smartphone's cold blue-cyan glow lights a rumpled white pillow and a relaxed hand loosely holding the phone. The face is completely out of frame or lost in deep shadow. The phone screen is an abstract soft blur of light with no readable content. 85mm lens, very shallow depth of field, focus on the fingertips and the edge of the phone, with the bedding falling into soft bokeh. Deep indigo shadows, cool blue key light from the screen, faint grain. Almost still, with only a subtle breathing movement of the hand. The mood is quiet, tired and tender. Leave negative space in the upper third for a caption.

assets.prompt: Reverent, painterly devotional scene in traditional Indian iconography, inspired by classical miniature and temple-painting styles. Lord Krishna is shown with a serene blue complexion, a peacock feather in his crown, a yellow pitambara garment and gentle jewellery, with a calm, compassionate expression. He is seated as charioteer at the front of an ornate wooden chariot drawn by white horses. Arjuna sits respectfully beside him in traditional warrior attire, with his bow resting, attentive and peaceful, listening. They are at the quiet edge of the field of Kurukshetra at dawn, and the field stretches away distant, empty and calm, with no conflict shown. A vast pale sky arches above them in peach, soft gold and pale blue, with soft clouds drifting slowly through it. Wide composition with the figures in the lower third and the sky dominant. Very subtle motion only: drifting clouds, a gentle breeze in the horses' manes and the fabric. Soft, luminous dawn light with a dignified, sacred and tranquil mood.

assets.prompt: Warm, gentle, unhurried narrator in their 30s with a soft neutral accent. Close-mic, intimate late-night tone, like speaking quietly to a friend who can't sleep. Calm and compassionate, never preachy. Natural pauses between sentences, slightly slower and reverent on the verse. Script: "It's 1 a.m. and you've read that one comment eleven times. Pause. Look up at the sky for a moment. [pause] Some words land hard. They sting. That's real, and it's okay that it hurts. [pause] In the Bhagavad Gita, Krishna offers Arjuna an image worth holding on a night like this. [pause] As the omnipresent ether is not affected, by reason of its subtlety, so seated everywhere in the body the Self is not affected. [pause] Teachers across many traditions read this as describing the Self: like space, it holds everything that passes through it, yet is not stained by any of it. [pause] A reflection, not scripture: that comment can reach your mind, and the mind may feel it. The Gita points to a deeper witness in you that those words do not touch. [pause] You don't have to pretend it didn't hurt. Just put the phone down. Breathe. Let it pass, like a cloud across the sky." Timing guide per scene: 6s, 7s, 7s, 10s, 8s, 9s, 8s.

assets.prompt: Calm ambient meditative score, about 60 BPM or free-time. A soft tanpura drone in D, warm low synth pads, distant airy textures, sparse felt-piano notes, and a very gentle bansuri flute phrase entering around the verse (≈20s) and swelling subtly at the dawn chariot scene (≈30–38s). Light shimmering high tones evoke a night sky and stars. No percussion and no drops. The mix stays low under the voiceover, and the track resolves into a soft sustained chord and fades out over the final 4 seconds. The mood is spacious, tender, reverent and reassuring.
